# Agent Joules build log

Purpose: the single record of toolchain facts, version deviations, scan results, test counts, per-ID filter results, probe and WSL2 notes, user actions, requirements that cannot be met and base commits (REQ-002, REQ-029, builder standing order 6). ASCII only, LF only; never a key value, a hostname or an IP. Every number carries one label: measured, user-reported, inferred or assumed.

## Toolchain check

Commands, exit codes, UTC dates and labels of the SDK, Docker, WSL2, Ollama, GPU driver and git checks (AJ-002), plus the hygiene, property and grep checks that later M0 stories run.

### AJ-001 checks (2026-10-18T16:17:53Z, measured)

| Check | Command | Exit code | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| nine headings once each | for each of the nine headings: `grep -cxF "<heading>" docs/build-log.md`; a count other than 1 prints `missing heading: <heading>` and the loop exits 1 | 0 | every count is 1 |
| ASCII only | `grep -nP "[^\x00-\x7F]" docs/build-log.md` | 1 | no match |
| LF only, story command | `grep -c $'\r' docs/build-log.md` | prints 0 | printed 0; the M0 peer reviewer measured that GNU grep 3.0 does count CR bytes when bash expands `$'\r'`, so a 0 on a CRLF file came from the executor's POSIX-sh shell not expanding `$'\r'`, not from grep; the byte count on the next row is the binding check |
| LF only, byte count | `tr -cd '\r' < docs/build-log.md` followed by `wc -c` | prints 0 | 0 CR bytes |
| no key pattern | `grep -nE "nvapi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}" docs/build-log.md` | 1 | no match |
| negative, scratch copy: deleted heading | the heading loop on a copy without `## Test counts` | 1 | printed `missing heading: ## Test counts` |
| negative, scratch copy: non-ASCII dash | `grep -nP "[^\x00-\x7F]"` on a copy with an em-dash appended | 0 | reported the offending line number (44) |
| scratch copy: a row appended under an existing heading | one row appended under `## Secret scan`, then `grep -cxF "## Secret scan"` | prints 1 | heading count unchanged, no new heading |

Working-tree line endings (2026-10-18T16:22Z, measured with `tr -cd '\r' < <file>` and `wc -c`): `.editorconfig` has 389 CR bytes in 389 lines and `.gitignore` 482 CR bytes in 499 lines, so both are CRLF in the working tree (`git ls-files --eol` prints `i/lf w/crlf`; `core.autocrlf=true`). README.md, .gitattributes and the docs/ files are LF. The index is LF for every file. Design section 2.3 states the worktree was LF on 2026-10-18; that is not true for these two files. AJ-009 adds `* text=auto eol=lf` and re-checks the two files out as LF.

## Version deviations and additions

Every package whose used version differs from the pins of design section 2.4 (package, pinned version, used version, reason) and every package added beyond the design list (REQ-002).

Decision (2026-10-18, AJ-005): stay on the prompt pins. The coordinator versions Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.11.0, Microsoft.Agents.AI 1.25.0 and OpenTelemetry 1.20.0 are rejected (design C-01, ADR-20 row 1, open point O-01). `dotnet restore` exit 0 on all 22 pins (measured 16:28Z and 16:36Z); no NuGet audit warning; no deviation recorded. M0 adds no package beyond design section 2.4; M1 story AJ-033 adds the Options packages and records them here as additions.

| Package | Pinned version | Used version | Reason |

Scan of record for AJ-011: `git grep fallback` (gitleaks not installed), exit code 1 (no match), verdict clean, measured first at commit 8635b32 (2026-10-18T16:48:49Z) and re-run at commit 71a1cf4 (2026-10-18T17:07:24Z) after the AJ-008, AJ-009 and AJ-010 commits that touched docs/ and tests/. Rule (broadened on the security reviewer's finding): the scan is re-run on the working tree before each commit until M7 (tracked, untracked and history greps, so the content about to be committed is covered), not only before commits that touch docs/ or config/, because test fixtures under tests/ and src/ are the likelier leak; the latest exit code is the one that counts; each re-run is appended as the next row of the table above, the M0 exit re-run included; future pattern re-runs use `-l` instead of `-n` so a hit prints only the file name. Known limits of the fallback against gitleaks: it cannot catch keys that are not in the current environment, credentials without the `nvapi-` prefix and without a registered value, encoded or split values, dangling objects, or high-entropy strings of unknown shape. Amended 2026-10-18 (post-exit review): the exact-value greps pass the value on stdin, `printf '%s\n' "${!NAME}" | git grep -qF -f -` (also with `--untracked` and over `$(git rev-list --all)`), never as a command-line argument, because an argument is visible in process listings and git traces while git runs; an empty value makes git grep exit 128, so the empty-variable guard stays.

## Probe and WSL2 notes

Results of `probe` runs and of the Linux and WSL2 execution checks (M1 and later).

Pre-measurement 2026-10-19T09:00Z (measured, for AJ-036 and AJ-037): `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name,power.limit --format=csv,noheader` printed `616.92, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU, [N/A]` (power.limit not reported by nvidia-smi in this mode); `docker manifest inspect mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0` exit 0 (the tag exists); `actionlint` is on PATH. WSL2: Ubuntu-22.04 has .NET SDKs 8.0.414 and 9.0.203 but no 10.0.4xx, so `dotnet` fails against the repository's global.json (10.0.401); Ubuntu has no dotnet; kali-linux has SDK 6.0.400 only; all three distros have `nvidia-smi` and `/usr/lib/wsl/lib/libnvidia-ml.so.1`. Conclusion for AJ-036-T4 (inferred): the WSL2 probe cannot run with the distro SDKs as installed; the story allows "not run: <reason>", and the library path confirms the design 5.6 inference that WSL2 exposes NVML under `/usr/lib/wsl/lib`.

Laptop NVML facts from the gated integration test (measured 2026-10-19T10:42Z and 10:43Z, AJ-023): name `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU`; driver `616.92`; `nvmlDeviceGetTotalEnergyConsumption` supported (rc 0), so the counter method is available on this GPU (design R-01 resolved; the prompt's UNVERIFIED row is now measured); `nvmlDeviceGetCurrentClocksEventReasons` supported (rc 0), so EDGE-013 throttle detection has data on this laptop and the AJ-028 criterion 7 sentence for the M4 methodology is "throttle reasons are supported on this GPU" (the unsupported sentence is not needed); MIG `not-supported` (rc 3); enforced power limit 91.210 W at 10:42Z and 88.554 W at 10:43Z (also 75.000 and 87.699 W earlier today, 85.059 W on 2026-10-18 by NVML, 94.62 W on 2026-10-17 by nvidia-smi): the limit moves with the laptop power mode within a minute, so no document quotes a fixed limit and the committed probe (AJ-037) is the authority at run time (design C-11). Two further limit readings: 93.711 W (code-review gate) and 95.283 W at 10:45Z (spec gate). AJ-028 criterion 7 is satisfied by this record: the throttle API is supported, and the AJ-028 Specs scenario reads this paragraph.

Probe output on the laptop (measured 2026-10-19, AJ-035): `probe` printed the ten lines: GPU name `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti Laptop GPU`, GPU UUID `GPU-7687512b...` (the first eight characters after the prefix; the rest not recorded), Driver version `616.92`, Compute capability `8.6`, VBIOS version `94.03.1b.00.3a`, Power limit W `87.867`, MIG mode `not-supported`, Energy counter supported `true`, Method `counter`, Sample rate Hz `10`; `probe --json` printed the eleven-key object with powerLimitW 87.619 on the second run; both exit 0 with empty stderr. The enforced power limit moved between two consecutive runs (87.867 W, then 87.619 W); the earlier readings in this section are 94.62 W (nvidia-smi, 2026-10-17), 85.059 W (NVML, 2026-10-18) and 75.000, 87.699, 91.210, 88.554, 93.711 and 95.283 W (NVML, 2026-10-19). ### AJ-010 Redact key values in any text output (REQ-029)

- Shipped: `src/AgentJoules.Core/Security/SecretRedactor.cs` (Register, Redact, the `nvapi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{4,}` pattern as a generated regex, longest-first registered values, the six-character reveal with the short-value rule, superseded by the follow-up entry below), `src/AgentJoules.Cli/Output/RedactingTextWriter.cs` (line-buffered TextWriter that redacts before anything reaches the inner writer; Flush and Dispose write the remainder), `tests/AgentJoules.UnitTests/RedactionTests.cs` (19 facts at that commit, 21 after the follow-up, trait Spec=REQ-029), `tests/AgentJoules.Specs/Features/Configuration/AJ-010-redact-key-values.feature` (the story's seven scenarios verbatim) and `tests/AgentJoules.Specs/Steps/ConfigurationSteps.cs`. Console wiring is AJ-034 (M1).
- Decisions: the regex runs before the registered values (a registered value such as `-` would otherwise split the `nvapi-` prefix and leak the suffix; found by the code review, fixed and guarded by a test); registered values are also registered trimmed, so a trailing CR from a CRLF file cannot leak the bare key; the writer owns and disposes its inner writer, passes FormatProvider and NewLine through, and is documented as not thread-safe (AJ-034 wraps it with TextWriter.Synchronized, one instance per stream); the first version of this commit kept the story's six-character reveal; the M0 peer review cited design-review N-09 (every other secret becomes `****`), so design 3.2 is the authority, the story text was superseded and the AJ-010 follow-up commit masks every registered value as `****` (entry below).
- Deviations: one step pattern in ConfigurationSteps.cs carried `^...$` anchors because Reqnroll parsed it as a Cucumber expression otherwise; the follow-up commit replaced that binding, so no binding is anchored now. - Security mitigation note (final wording from the security gate, 2026-10-19; also placed in design 5.6):

  Linux and WSL2 (inferred for the cloudgpu VM; measured in Docker on the laptop): the resolver passes `libnvidia-ml.so.1`, then `libnvidia-ml.so`, to `NativeLibrary.TryLoad(name, out h)`, which hands the soname to `dlopen` unchanged. The dynamic loader then searches `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, the executable's `DT_RUNPATH`, `/etc/ld.so.cache` (on WSL2 this includes `/usr/lib/wsl/lib` through `/etc/ld.so.conf.d`), then `/lib` and `/usr/lib`. The .NET host's native-library folders, including the application folder of a self-contained publish, are not probed. When neither soname loads, the resolver throws `DllNotFoundException`, so the runtime's default search never runs. Anyone who can set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` can already inject code through `LD_PRELOAD` or `DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS`, so no privilege boundary is crossed. Operating rules: run the CLI as an unprivileged user, never as root; never run it with an `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` that contains an empty entry or `.`, because `dlopen` reads those as the current directory; keep `artifacts/linux-x64` on the VM writable only by the deploying user.

  Windows (measured 2026-10-19): `nvml.dll` is loaded by its full path under `Environment.SystemDirectory`. Its static imports are `KERNEL32.dll` and `ADVAPI32.dll` only, both KnownDLLs, so its dependencies never come from the current directory or PATH. The NVSMI fallback is tried only when `ProgramW6432` is a fully qualified path and the System32 copy fails to load. Anyone who controls the environment can already run code in the process.
- Carried forward: AJ-022 builds the `Unavailable` reason from fixed text naming `nvml.dll` or `libnvidia-ml.so.1`, never from the exception message, because the resolver's message lists the full load paths including whatever `ProgramW6432` held (security advisory); the story that adds kernel32 imports to this assembly (`PowerSourceDetector`, design 3.1) must route them to System32 full paths too, since `Resolve` returns zero for other names and the runtime default search probes the host folders first (security advisory); the deprecated-export reader path is proven at the reader level only, the laptop driver has the new export (code-review and spec remark); `Resolve`'s throw path, the NVSMI branch and the Linux branch have not run on the laptop host itself, the Linux branch is measured in Docker (above). A short registered key value (five characters or more) that occurs in a run file or a rendered output refuses the report with nothing written, fail-closed by design; real keys are long random strings (AJ-086 gates, owner: the user at the M3 exit, only if a placeholder key is ever registered).

- Decisions: the orchestrator pinned these before the build. The real `run` command is AJ-054's, so the five scenarios run through the stand-in `PreflightRunCommand` and `RunCommandStandIn` with the real preflight, catalog client and provider pipeline, precedent AJ-052 and AJ-055. The design's composite `CheckAsync(tiers, dryRun)` and `DryRunService` stay with AJ-054. The ID lines are printed by the command through `ConsoleReporter.ReportModelNotFound`, because `ErrorLine` folds an exception message into one line. The judge model check is skipped outside dry-run when the judge key is missing (that path already warned under AJ-052 criterion 5). Provider-returned IDs are redacted and then echoed before they enter a message (the carry-over from the AJ-049 and AJ-052 gates); matching is done on echoed IDs on both sides, so a long ID or one with a control character still matches itself. `ModelIdListFormatter.Format` keeps at most 20 IDs, places every ID containing nemotron or qwen (case-insensitive) first, keeps provider order otherwise, and keeps the total count. The check stops at the first failing tier. The EDGE-008 tests live in a nested class so that the AJ-052 class trait does not tag them. Fix round decisions: matching is exact on the IDs as the provider wrote them and echoing is for display only, so two IDs sharing their first 64 characters or differing in a control character stay apart (the round-1 code review measured the collision with two 68-character GGUF tags); the key never leaves `ProviderClientFactory` (`CreateModelsRequest`); the preflight GET is capped at 30 s because a models listing is small and `--tier all` would otherwise wait up to 300 s per tier; the header count comes from the distinct raw IDs while the shown list is distinct after echo, so the header can read `first 4 of 5` when two raw IDs display the same (accepted, cosmetic, noted by the spec and security reviewers); a missing ID and a listed ID that share their first 64 characters display the same cut text in the error line and the list while the exit code is right (accepted; a longer echo length for model IDs is a possible later change); a non-2xx answer from `/models`, including 401, exits 5, not 3 (the spec does not cover it; recorded).

### AJ-056 Orchestrate a tier run over tasks, repeats and modes (REQ-017, REQ-013, EDGE-005)

- Shipped (builder 12:28Z to 13:07Z, tests written first; battery 1 13:09:23Z to 13:11:27Z): replaced the `RunOrchestrator` placeholder with the production orchestrator. Per selected tier it builds the `MeteringServices` (`SampledEnergyMeter` over the GPU opened again at `Gpu:Index` for `local` and `cloudgpu`, `UnmeteredEnergyMeter` for `nvidia` and `nebius`; the `IMeterGate` chosen by `--mode`; one in-memory sink per tier run, forwarded to `IRunListener`), with `ICostCalculator`, `AgentJoulesInstruments` and the host `TimeProvider`. A measured tier runs the start sequence (GPU port, meter start, warm-up once per distinct model ID, idle baseline for `--baseline-seconds` with `Baseline:MaxCoefficientOfVariation`, the EDGE-005 warning through `ConsoleReporter.ReportBaseline` on stderr). Then every task in file order and every repeat 1..n runs with fresh agents (`AgentFactory.CreateAll`) and a fresh workflow (`AgentJoulesWorkflowFactory.RunAsync`), one `running` checkpoint after each (task, repeat) and a final `completed` write; the meter and the GPU source are disposed in a `finally`. Shutdown (Ctrl+C, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, `ApplicationStopping`): each `cancelled` reading of the interrupted (task, repeat) is copied as `incomplete`, `run.status` becomes `incomplete`, the checkpoint is written with a fresh 10 s wall-clock token, then the cancellation is rethrown and the command exits 5. A shutdown before the first step still writes an incomplete file holding the probe. A `StepFailedException` propagates (exit 5). `RunAssembler` builds the `RunDocument` (run id, tasks, mode, repeat, `startUtc`, tool version and commit, environment, models, totals with labels, checkpoints that carry the totals so far). `ConsoleRunListener` (the Cli implementation of `IRunListener`) prints one line per finished step and the `results:` and `totals:` lines per tier through `ConsoleReporter`. `ReportSentences.ConcurrentOverlap` holds the fixed concurrent-overlap sentence. Seams: `IJudgeService` with `NoOpJudgeService`, `ILocalRuntime` with `LocalRuntimeInfo` and `NoOpLocalRuntime`. The run command's service hook registers the meter gate, the agent factory and `AgentJoulesInstruments` beside the telemetry; `RunPlan` gained `StartUtc` and `OutputDisplay`; `RunCommand` takes the start instant once for every tier's file name. P-4: one pipeline per judgeable step, built like `AgentFactory` (provider client of `Judge:Tier`, `RateLimitRetryChatClient`, `MeteredChatClient` outermost with one shared `RetryLedger`), identity `Judge` with `JudgedAgent`, one buffered call at Temperature 0, disposed after the call. P-5: `StepIdentity` and `StepReading` gain the optional `JudgedAgent`, written only when non-null, so a judge reading names the agent whose output it scored and no `JudgeReading` type exists. P-6: `totals.judge` keeps tokens and `costByCurrency` only; a hosted judge's N/A `hosted-tier` shows on each judge reading, never as 0 and never summed. P-7: `JudgeService` writes the reason table on its returned copy through `RunAssembler.WithQuality` with `qualityReason` `not-scored` on every unscored row and leaves the derived metrics to `Assemble`. P-8: `JudgeService` owns the four-case rule (`step-not-ok` and `empty-output` without a call, the judge call for the rest), and the orchestrator passes every step and writes no quality. P-9: `selfJudged` is the ordinal equality of `Judge:ModelId` with any request step's ModelId, passed to `BuildRunInfo` for the completed write only and null otherwise. - Deviations: D1, `Select` stops at the first accepted file per (tier, variant), newest first, so `Skipped` and `Problems` list only files newer than the winner, and every file when none is accepted (a corrupt file older than the winner is not reported; test `Files_older_than_the_selected_one_are_not_opened`); the reason is that the report never needs an older file, the story's criterion 2 does not say what the lists must hold, and the design and story record it. D2, `Select` throws `ArgumentException` for a blank input and for an input that is neither a folder nor a name satisfying `RunFileName.IsValid` (the name echoed through `TextEcho`), and `ArgumentNullException` for a null list, while a valid-named missing file and an unlistable folder are the Problem `unreadable`; the reason is that P-25 has the command check names and existence first, so these are contract guards, and `Select` resolves relative paths against the process directory, so AJ-086 passes absolute paths. D3, `Latest` and `LatestBaseline` read only the requested tier, an invalid tier gives `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` through `TierOptions.NameOf`, a missing folder gives `DirectoryNotFoundException`, and the first Problem of that tier throws `InvalidDataException("<file>: <reason>")` (the draft P-1 wording). D4, header reader details beyond P-2: a `run` that is null or not an object is `run-missing`; a `tier` or `status` that is not a string is `tier-unknown` or `status-unknown`; the last of duplicate `tier`, `status` or `flags` members inside `run`, and the first of duplicate top-level `run` members; a JSON error or invalid UTF-8 is `header-not-json`; at exactly 64 KiB one more byte is probed to tell `header-too-long` from `header-not-json`; the reason is that the reviewers verify the bound before any larger read. D5, the values of `Latest` and `LatestBaseline` are full paths; `Skipped` and `Problems` carry the file name only, ordered ordinally by file name, then by reason. D6, the tier-mismatch check runs before the status rule, so a failed file of the wrong tier is a Problem, not a Skip, and a failed or incomplete status wins over `non-publishable` as the skip reason. D7, the Specs steps run the real selector on files built from the committed fixture text with status and flags edited in a TempWorkspace, the unit tests use minimal header texts, and one unit test points `Select` at the committed fixtures folder in place. D8 (two scratchpad files created and deleted, none in the repository) is a note, not a deviation. D9 (fix round), a FIFO named like a run file is `header-not-json` rather than `unreadable` on Unix, because .NET exposes no file type and a FIFO, a character device and an empty file all report size 0, so the size-0 rule refuses all three before any open; the reason is that a read of a FIFO would block. D10 (fix round), there is no pre-open check on Windows, because a named pipe reports as an empty regular file there and only `CanSeek` tells it apart after the open, so the refusal is `unreadable` at that point.

### M0 review2: suggestions, question and nitpicks of the final full-depth review (REQ-001, REQ-029)

- Shipped on branch milestone/M0-review2: `SecretRedactor.TrimEnds` returns a slice of the original string, decoding runes from both ends and keeping any invalid sequence (a lone surrogate) as visible, so the ends-trimmed form masks a raw echo of a malformed configured value; `RemoveInvisibleCharacters` drops invalid sequences for the clean form; `Register` registers the whole value and each of its CR- or LF-separated lines in up to three forms each (ends-trimmed, clean, rune-normalised with U+FFFD for an echo that passed through UTF-8), after the security gate showed that rejecting a multi-line value whole left a key on one of its lines unmasked and the code-review gate showed that per-line registration alone dropped short lines and newline-stripped echoes; the `RedactingTextWriter` summary is reflowed to 120 columns and states that a leaveOpen writer stays usable after Dispose and drains on every later Dispose (the AJ-034 console wrappers may receive output after the first drain and before the ProcessExit drain) while an owning writer throws; the generic Reqnroll step "the result is ..." asserts exact equality only; `tests/AgentJoules.Specs/Features/Configuration/.gitkeep` deleted because the folder holds a feature file; fifteen tests added over three gate rounds, two of them theories over the seven line terminators (61 cases on Spec=REQ-029). (3) Measured on this laptop in 1 of 40 runs: in serialized mode the branch waiting on the meter gate can receive the gate after the shutdown ended the held branch's call, open a window and fail at once on the cancelled token, so a third step is recorded `incomplete`; `AssertIncomplete`, `Shutdown_marks_in_flight_steps_incomplete` and the Specs Ctrl+C step now assert the invariant through `RunOrchestrationFixtures.AssertShutdownDuringFirstFanOut` (2 or 3 steps of the same task and repeat 1, the Planner first and `ok`, every other step a distinct Researcher or Writer with outcome `incomplete`, no Reviewer and no later task or repeat, the console listing the same steps in file order), with `run.status` `incomplete`, exit 5, the single error line and the time bound unchanged. - 2026-10-24, after the exit (user-requested probes with the NVIDIA sample request shape, two Nano ids, no key prefix in any output): `nvidia/nemotron-nano-3-30b-a3b` returns 404 "Function ... Not found for account" with the exact sample body too (stream, thinking enabled, a reasoning budget), so decision 2 stands as an account entitlement. The "empty completions" of the live runs are explained: a streamed call to `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning` returned HTTP 200 whose event stream held one chunk `{"error":{"message":"ResourceExhausted: Worker local total request limit reached (16/16)","type":"internal_server_error","code":500}}` and then `[DONE]`; our streaming client reads only `choices`, so the step was recorded as outcome ok with 0 output chars (quality N/A `empty-output`, no retry). The same model answered the same prompt a moment later with 92 completion tokens (reasoning and content both present). The judge failures of about 130 ms with ClientResultException on the buffered path are consistent with the same saturated free-tier worker returning the error as an HTTP status. Decision 3 is therefore reworded: a stream chunk carrying an `error` object must end the step as a provider error (outcome error with the type and code, never ok), and a transient ResourceExhausted must enter the retry policy like a 429; owner M4 (AJ-104 messages and the live campaign), to be built before any published run. Probe bodies in the m3-live-run folder of the session scratchpad.
- 2026-10-24 14:06Z to 14:07Z, run 4 (user-requested, `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning` for the agents and the judge, inline overrides, nothing committed, no key prefix anywhere): exit 0, status completed; the Planner returned the ResourceExhausted error chunk again (recorded ok, 0 chars, quality N/A `empty-output`); Researcher, Writer and Reviewer ok with 384 output tokens each; the judge call for the Researcher returned 32 tokens of visible reasoning ("We need to judge the output...") and ended as `parse-error`, exactly the failure mode stated in decision 2 (r-3), because `ReasoningMode: off` is recorded in the environment facts and never sent (no `SystemPromptPrefix` for the nvidia tier, no thinking switch anywhere in src); the judge calls for the Writer and Reviewer failed in 125 and 162 ms with ClientResultException. Three buffered probes with a judge-like 32-token request to the same model: the default body got HTTP 503 `ResourceExhausted: Worker local total request limit reached (16/16)` (so the judge's fast ClientResultExceptions are the saturated free-tier worker and should be retried like a 429); `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}` got 200 with 3 tokens and the digit; a system message `/no_think` got 200 with 3 tokens, the digit and an empty think wrapper. Consequence for decision 2: the omni-reasoning sibling is usable today without code change by setting `Tiers:nvidia:ModelId`, `Judge:ModelId` and `Tiers:nvidia:SystemPromptPrefix` (`/no_think`, which the agents and, since the exit fix, the judge send as the system message); M4 adds the `enable_thinking` field behind `ReasoningMode` and the retry for 500 and 503 ResourceExhausted (owner M4, with decision 3).
